title: I built an AI game dev studio — 6 specialized agents, real quality gates, and it actually ships games
author: Public-Profession588
selftext:
# I want to share something I've been building: Game Dev Studio — an AI-powered multi-agent workspace that simulates a real game development studio process, from game design all the way to QA-gated delivery.

**TL;DR**: It's not a code autocomplete. It's 6 AI agents (Game Designer, CEO, Architect, Engineer, Biz Designer, Team Builder) collaborating through structured handoff workflows. Games go through a real lint pipeline (SonarQube + 20 custom engineering rules) before they can be submitted. Think of it as a miniature game company where every employee is an LLM.

# What it actually does

You start a project, and the agents handle the full pipeline:

1. **Game Designer** creates a design proposal (non-technical users can use a structured questionnaire form)
2. **CEO** reviews and approves it
3. **Architect** designs the system architecture
4. **Engineer** builds the game — with access to Blender (3D), Draw.io (diagrams), and ImageMagick (image processing) tools
5. **Biz Designer** handles business planning
6. **Team Builder** consolidates learnings after every session

Every game submission is gated by:

* **SonarQube** static analysis (quality gate failure = blocked)
* **Game Engineering Checker**: 20 rules validating HTML structure, metadata schema, lifecycle contracts, asset manifests, and resource paths
* Three game type specs: HTML5, Phaser Mobile (with Capacitor), and common rules for all types

# Tech stack

|Layer|Stack|
|:-|:-|
|Backend|Node.js + Express + TypeScript|
|Frontend|React 18 + Vite + Tailwind + TDesign|
|AI SDK|/tencent-ai/agent-sdk (MCP-based)|
|DB|SQLite via better-sqlite3 (WAL mode)|
|Object Storage|MinIO (S3-compatible)|
|Microservices|FastAPI × 4 (Blender, Draw.io, ImageMagick, SonarQube Scanner)|
|E2E Testing|Playwright (10 scenarios, 90% coverage)|
|CI|GitHub Actions|

All services run in Docker Compose — single `make compose-build` to get everything up.

# Architecture that I'm genuinely proud of

The entire system runs on **MCP (Model Context Protocol) custom tools** — \~50+ tools form the complete API surface. Agents never call REST endpoints directly; everything flows through typed tool schemas with Zod validation.

**Event-driven UI**: All state changes (proposals, game submissions, handoffs) broadcast via SSE. The React frontend subscribes to a single `/api/observe` stream — every panel stays in sync without polling.

**Extensible lint pipeline**: New checkers implement a `LintChecker` interface, register in one array, and they're automatically included in every game submission. Rules are also scoped by game type, so HTML5 games get 14 rules while Phaser Mobile games get 20.

**Project scoping by design**: Tools don't accept `project_id` as a parameter — the backend injects it at initialization. You physically cannot cross-project tamper.

# The "why" behind this

I got tired of AI coding tools that just dump code. Real software development — especially game dev — involves design, review, architecture planning, asset creation, and quality assurance. I wanted to model that full workflow.

What makes this different from "ask ChatGPT to write a game":

1. **Role specialization with forced handoffs** — the engineer physically cannot approve a design proposal. Only the CEO can. This creates genuine review steps.
2. **Asset pipeline integration** — the engineer agent can call Blender to create 3D models, Draw.io for diagrams, ImageMagick for sprites. These aren't simulated; they're real Dockerized services producing real files.
3. **Quality gates that block bad output** — if your game fails SonarQube or misses required lifecycle methods, the submission is rejected. No "it compiles, ship it" nonsense.
4. **Non-technical accessibility** — the questionnaire system lets designers contribute without writing code.

# What it looks like

The frontend is a dashboard with:

* Agent runtime panel (live status + logs per agent)
* Project tabs (proposals, games, handoffs, task board, architecture diagrams)
* Real-time event stream
* Game artifact viewer with SonarQube report download
* Star-Office integration panel

15 technical specs (SPEC-001 through SPEC-016) document the project evolution. 11 are implemented, 4 are in design (video service, build service, run service, test service).

# What it's NOT

* Not a game engine (games are HTML5/Phaser-based, run in browser or Capacitor)
* Not a consumer product (it's a development platform)
* Not trying to replace game developers (it's a tool to accelerate them)

# State of the project

✅ Core multi-agent workflow with 6 roles ✅ 5 Dockerized microservices ✅ SonarQube + Game Engineering lint pipeline ✅ Proposal questionnaire for non-technical users ✅ Blender 3D, Draw.io diagram, ImageMagick image tools 🚧 Video processing service (design phase)

It's open source and actively developed.

Happy to answer questions about the multi-agent architecture, the MCP tool design. Also open to brutal feedback — I built this to solve real problems.

**GitHub**: It's on luoxiaojun1992's repos (search "game-studio") **Stack**: TypeScript, React, Express, FastAPI, Docker, Playwright, SonarQube, MinIO, Blender **License**: Open source
